Solutions for Level C: Inventory.

Concept Overview

  • Composition: The Player "has a" Inventory (not "is a").
  • Encapsulation: The list `_items` is hidden. We interact via `add()`, `remove()`.
  • Static/Class Variables: `MAX_CAPACITY` belongs to the blueprint.

Common Misconceptions

1. `self._items` vs `item`

Students confuse the list with the single item. `add(item)` appends to `self._items`.

2. Returning True/False

The spec requires boolean returns. Students often just `print("Added")` which breaks the logical tests.

Solution Code

class Inventory:
    MAX_CAPACITY = 10  # Class variable

    def __init__(self):
        self._items = []  # Private list

    def add(self, item_id):
        if len(self._items) >= Inventory.MAX_CAPACITY:
            return False
        if item_id in self._items:
            return False
        self._items.append(item_id)
        return True

    def remove(self, item_id):
        if item_id in self._items:
            self._items.remove(item_id)
            return True
        return False

    def list_items(self):
        return self._items[:]  # Return a COPY (Encapsulation)

    def has_item(self, item_id):
        return item_id in self._items
